full_judgment: 60. The petitioners denied to have received any of the letters. They further said that their office was transferred to the Rangs Bhaban before 1998. To prove service, the said respondents annexed photo copy of the acknowledgments to their supplementary affidavit. It appears therefrom that on 08-08-99 someone on behalf of the petitioners received the mail. But in the mail, the petitioners were addressed to be of 28 Purina Paltan, Dhaka. Another mail addressed to 68 Purana Paltan appears to he received on 13-09-98 by one A. Rahim on behalf of the petitioners. The sanction letter was issued to the petitioners to the address of 68, Purana Paltan. Dhaka. The respondents wanted to rely on the acknowledgment dated 08-04-99 to say that the notice for show cause dated 08-04-99 was sent by the said mail and received by the petitioners. But no record was produced to prove that the petitioners were ever housed at 28 Purana Paltan. So, when the mail was not properly addressed, there is hardly any scope for holding any valid presumption of good service. Section 27 of the General Clauses Act may be referred to. Besides, there could not be any earthly reason for the petitioners whose stake is so heavy in the construction of the building to keep silent even after receipt of those letters.
